Everfresh · Grow Chamber v2

The Vitrine

A Living Showpiece Cabinet
A warm-wood-frame, all-glass grow cabinet on casters — built to grow one Cojoba angustifolia hard, and to be beautiful doing it.
~24 × 18 × 52 in  •  ~$200 + LED  •  ~10-day build
The Idea

A cabinet the tree lives in

v1 was a wire rack wrapped in taped plastic — leaky, fogged, awkward to open, and no one's idea of a centerpiece. v2 flips the goal: a glass-on-all-four-sides conservatory cabinet that reads as furniture. More room for the leader that's already arching for the light, a full front door for easy daily access, and the glowing tree as the whole point of the room.

Interior
24×18×52 in
Volume
~14.6 cu ft
Cabinet budget
~$200 +LED
Timeline
~10 days
Priorities, in order
1  More room 2  Easy access + beautiful 3  Leak-sealing 4  Insulation (out by design)

Glass on all sides means insulation can't come along — and it's your last priority anyway. The trade: heat & light spill to the room (the glow is the feature). Keep the west window shaded for the 4–8 PM solar spike, still the highest-leverage thermal fix.

Anatomy

How it all fits

1
Active top exhaust

PC fan in a port cut to the fan body (foam collar, no short-circuit) — the peak-shaver during the afternoon solar spike.

2
Full-spectrum white LED

Sleek dimmable panel under the top; driver hidden in the attic. Warm daylight glow, not blurple.

3
Circulation fan

Blows down to mix the gradient; gentle continuous trickle between cycles.

4
Canopy sensor

SHT31 at leaf height — the control point every decision uses.

5
Reptile heat bulb

Mid-level above the reservoir, radiating up. Your proven heat source.

6
The tree

Cojoba angustifolia — room to reach ~3 ft before the next rebuild.

7
Fogger + reservoir

Humidity source; refill through the front door.

8
Waterproof base pan

Sealed, sloped to a corner — catches fog-spit + condensation.

9
Passive intake + outdoor sensor

Low screened port; second SHT31 reads the air the exhaust pulls in.

10
Sealed attic

All electronics — exhaust fan, LED driver, Photon — out of the humid zone.

Systems

What carries over & what changes

Keep from v1Change for v2
Fogger + reservoir (humidity)Drop heat mat & intentional floor pool
Reptile heat bulb, mid-level, radiating upGrow light → sleek dimmable white LED
Circ fan up top, blowing downEnclosure → wood + glass vitrine
Passive low intake + active top exhaustAccess: taped flap → full swing door
2× SHT31 (canopy + intake) · PhotonHidden waterproof base pan for runoff

No firmware changes needed — sensor roles, actuators, and airflow direction are all unchanged.

Lighting — white, not blurple

  • ViparSpectra P1000 ~$100 — recommended
  • Mars Hydro TS600 ~$70 — value
  • Barrina bars ~$35 — sleekest

Dimmable (hormesis tuning). Driver in the attic. Target ~200–400 PPFD.

Seal the leaks

  • EPDM bulb gasket around the door
  • Compression / roller latch pulls it tight
  • Panels bedded in 100% silicone
  • All wires via sealed glands in the attic

Aesthetic — warm & tropical

  • Frame: Douglas fir (honey) or cedar (rot-resistant, reddish); sapele if you splurge
  • Finish: teak/Danish oil → spar urethane — warmth + waterproofs the wood in lieu of a liner
  • Hardware: brass hinge, handle & latch — conservatory feel
Airflow — the negative-pressure box
A

Passive intake, low — a screened port draws room air in at the base.

→
B

Circ fan pushes down — mixes the gradient; heat bulb warms the rising column.

→
C

Active exhaust, top — pulls stale/hot air out; the afternoon peak-shaver.

Sealed tight, this finally lets the CO₂ vent schedule come back on — the airflow goal v1 never quite reached.

The Build

Budget & plan

ItemEst.
Acrylic, 1/8″ (3/16″ door), ~30 sq ft cut to size — TAP Plastics$90
Frame wood — Douglas fir / cedar (2×2 posts, 1×2 rails)$40
Casters ×4 (2 locking)$18
Piano hinge + brass handle + latch$22
EPDM bulb weatherstrip$10
Silicone ×2 + glue + fasteners$15
Teak oil + spar urethane$20
Cabinet total (LED separate)~$215
Build sequence
1Order/cut acrylic at TAP (lead time — first)
2Mill + dry-fit frame; cut joinery + panel rabbets
3Finish wood (oil + spar) before glazing
4Build base pan + attic; cut exhaust/intake ports
5Glaze panels in silicone; hang door + gasket + latch
6Fogger leak-check by eye before wiring
7Mount LED, fans, heat bulb, fogger, sensors
8Power up, seal-test, tune

Three calls to lock it

  1. Footprint — 24×18 (my pick) or 20×20 square?
  2. LED — ViparSpectra P1000 (recommended), TS600, or Barrina bars?
  3. Frame wood — Douglas fir (cheap, honey), cedar (rot-proof), or sapele (splurge)?
